description: The graph illustrates the relationship between the loss ratio (%) and the number of TFLOPs for various models, including Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The x-axis represents the number of TFLOPs on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, while the y-axis shows the loss ratio in percentage, ranging from 94% to 100%. Each model is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker style. The Vanilla model is depicted by a purple line with square markers, showing a relatively stable loss ratio around 99.5% across the range of TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64) model is represented by an orange line with triangle markers, starting at approximately 98.5% and increasing to around 99.8% as TFLOPs increase. The SepLLM (n=128) model, shown with a blue line and star markers, begins at about 97.5% and rises to nearly 100%. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model, indicated by a green line with diamond markers, starts at around 97% and increases to approximately 99.5%. Lastly, the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model, represented by a red line with circle markers, starts at 94% and shows a significant increase to about 99.5% as TFLOPs increase. Overall, the graph demonstrates that all models exhibit an increase in loss ratio with higher TFLOPs, with the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model showing the most dramatic improvement.
